details.biography:
Lord Mayor-Free City of Greyhawk

AC 5 (leather armor and dexterity bonus); MV 12"; T 10; hp 45; #AT 1; Dmg by weapon type (proficient with sling, longsword, or dagger); Str 10, Int 11, Wis 8, Dex 17, Con 12, Cha 16; THAC0 8; AL LN; SA quadruple damage from backstab; SD high dexterity, thiefly skills

Nerof Gasgal was born to desperately poor but proud parents in one of the worst slums of Greyhawk. However hard they tried to talk him out of it, he idolized the Guild thieves, admiring their courage, their skill and above all their wealth. When he was ten his parents starved to death, and he resolved to change his fate. A family friend who was a Guild official sponsored him, and he became an apprentice of the Thieves' Guild.

Once a full thief he rose quickly, known for planning every last detail of a job. He left nothing to chance and would study plans and models of a target until he could draw its whole floor plan from memory. His thoroughness made him popular with his superiors and equals, though he terrified the apprentices and low-level thieves who worked under him, since he would not tolerate mistakes.

Then a terrible experience changed his career and his life. While looting a wizard's long-abandoned castle he set off a magic trap and found himself falling down an air shaft. Luckily the trap was an illusion, but his fellow thieves found him in a catatonic state and carried him back to Greyhawk. Clerics saved him, but he began to suffer severe dizzy spells and a fear of falling, and the incident convinced him to give up thieving and go into politics.

The public never knew Nerof as a thief. To them he was the owner of a gambling house for Greyhawk's wealthy young people. The games openly favored the house, yet he was popular with the newly rich, who had long urged him to run for office and promised their support. When his disability forced him to stop stealing, he took them up on it and was delighted with the opportunities he found.

As mayor he is popular and respected. His eye for detail makes it hard for anyone out of his favor to cheat or oppress the citizens. He demands a lot of his staff but no less of himself, working twelve-hour days as a matter of course. He takes bribes freely, but his rule is to "let both sides pay bribes, then judge the case on its merits."

His goals as mayor are to make the city run as smoothly as possible and to be remembered as its best Lord Mayor ever. Privately, he wants to join the aristocracy. The old rich do not think of him as the new rich do, and they snub him as much as they dare, for his lower-class accent and the "vulgar" source of his fortune, the gaming house. The nobles sneer at him in secret, but no one has forgotten what happened to one wealthy family foolish enough to shun him in public: thieves raided their house again and again, several family members died mysteriously, and their business rivals seemed to know all their plans, until the whole family was reduced to begging.

Nerof is an attractive, charming man, 5'9", with graying hair. He wears clothes of conservative cut but enormous cost, and looks like a trustworthy, capable businessman in politics only for the good of the city he loves.

His office is full of luxuries: heavy drapes (which hide the fact that it is several stories above the ground), several attractive secretaries, and a large, elaborate safe holding all the city files and plenty of information for blackmailing troublemakers he would rather not use force against. His leather armor is of the finest quality, custom-made by the head of the Leatherworkers' Guild after Nerof excused the leatherworkers from taxes during a severe leather shortage. His weapons are also the best there are, stolen for him by the Thieves' Guildmaster as a gift on his election. He owns a set of thieves' tools and still practices every thief skill that does not involve climbing. He can get many magic items but keeps few on hand unless he needs them, feeling that relying on a magic tool or weapon would make him too vulnerable. When he does use magic, he prefers items that help with theft without flying or climbing. There is a 20% chance of finding such items in his office or safe.

Outside politics his only interests are his gaming house, which he still owns, and keeping his thief skills sharp. He climbs socially but finds parties dull and goes for information. Like every mayor he keeps on good terms with the city's Guildmasters, but the only one he spends time with is the Thieves' Guildmaster; they often pass evenings over wine telling stories of the "good old days." Nerof is still a power in the Thieves' Guild and holds the title of Assistant Guildmaster.

Player characters might meet him as envoys from a neighboring land with business for the Lord Mayor, or as low-level thieves seeking his expert advice. He pays very well for information about outside threats to Greyhawk, and he is keen to buy magic items, especially ones useful to thieves, such as gauntlets of dexterity or chimes of opening. Enemies of Greyhawk will find him a deadly foe. He keeps close ties with the Assassins' Guildmaster, has several assassins on his private payroll, and has been known to use them to remove threats quietly.

GA p.35. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed. The armor class, THAC0 and damage are as printed; the sheet works out its own from the class, abilities and equipment.

Constable-Free City of Greyhawk

AC 3 (full plate + shield, dexterity penalty); MV 6" in armor; C 12; hp 58; #AT 1; Dmg by weapon type (flail, mace, staff of striking, staff sling, lasso); Str 13, Int 10, Wis 17, Dex 4, Con 16, Cha 16; THAC0 13; AL NG; SA Spells: 8-1st, 7-2nd, 6-3rd, 3-4th, 2-5th, 2-6th

Derider Fanshen was born to middle-class parents in Greyhawk. From early childhood she loved healing sick creatures, and she innocently annoyed her parents by filling the house with every sick or injured animal she found. Her gift and love for healing caught the eye of the priests of Pelor, god of the sun, strength, light and healing, who offered to train her. Her parents were overjoyed, both at the honor and at the prospect of a normal household at last.

As a novice of Pelor she learned fast and quickly became a full (1st level) cleric. When she was ordained she accepted an invitation to join a party of adventurers. Her superiors were sorry to see her go, since they loved her, but also relieved, because she was famous not just for her talent but for her clumsiness. She was always truly sorry about her accidents and was incapable of malice, but no apology mended the mirrors, jars and other fragile things she was forever dropping. While she was at the temple her superiors seriously thought of hiring a low-level wizard just to keep breakage down.

She adventured for several years, traveling the length and breadth of Oerth with her friends. She rose quickly, growing in confidence and in faith as she saw her prayers answered. But her clumsiness haunted her; she began to feel that fragile things were just waiting for her to drop them. Her companions loved her and were very patient, but when she dropped and smashed a beaker of plentiful potions the day after tripping while carrying a decanter of endless water, they gently suggested that adventuring might not be for her.

Back in Greyhawk she found that the temple of Pelor needed a cleric who specialized in healing. She was hired at once, on condition that she solemnly swear never to touch anything breakable (the high priest had been a classmate and knew her weakness). She was happy there, and her adventuring experience proved valuable when a band of undead plagued the temple district. Her work among the poor brought her to the notice of the Directing Oligarchy, and when a constable died after she had nursed him devotedly, she was offered the post.

As Constable she is a voice for mercy and moderation in the city government, and the whole Oligarchy trusts her to care for them when they are sick or hurt. Her clumsiness has not left her, but the Oligarchs can afford to be more tolerant of breakage than the priests or her old companions. When she tripped on her robe and knocked over a table of very expensive glassware, they simply chuckled and sent for a wizard to repair it.

She is a tall, attractive woman in her early forties, with tan skin, honey-blond hair and bright gray eyes. She is in excellent shape and looks much younger than she is. She has never married, preferring friendships with the important men in her life. Though retired from adventuring, she keeps her armor in good repair and exercises daily in it with her weapons, all souvenirs of her adventures, about which she happily tells stories. Her favorite is a staff of striking that also works as a staff sling +1.

Her goal as Constable is simple: keep the city safe and secure. Her family and her old adventuring friends live in Greyhawk, and she feels her duty to them keenly. She keeps in touch with them and is a popular party guest, once the breakables are safely put away.

The poor of Greyhawk often leave petitions at her house, asking her to speak for friends and relatives facing the city's justice. She does what she can, and Sental Nurev, Captain-General of the Watch, often has to remind her that her decision alone does not settle a criminal's fate. But she is no fool. Real evildoers know better than to ask her help, since she hates cruelty and wanton malice, having seen too much of both. The only time she shows anger is when some flagrant, unprovoked wrong comes to her attention, and then the people and the Oligarchy both take notice. She seldom uses spells for anything but healing, but she still can, and the anger of a 12th level cleric is nothing to invite.

Player characters might meet her through business with the Directing Oligarchy, since she attends its meetings; she has a soft spot for adventurers, and a party with a real need for the Oligarchy's help might find her willing to plead their case. They might also meet her by letting her know that a party member is sick or hurt but cannot pay for a cleric. Her adventuring made her financially secure, so she can indulge the same urge that troubled her parents long ago, healing every stray she comes across. She is known to vanish into the slums for days at a time, healing every sick or injured person she finds.

Captain-General of the Watch-Free City of Greyhawk

AC 3 (splint mail and shield); MV 9"; F 13; hp 85; #AT 2/1; Dmg by weapon type (lasso, halberd, man catcher, longsword, bo stick, jo stick, crossbow, club); Str 16, Int 12, Wis 15, Dex 13, Con 13, Cha 14; THAC0 8; AL NG

Sental Nurev was born near Greyhawk to poor country gentlefolk. Young as he was, he decided his skill with weapons was the only way out of poverty. A neighbor who had retired from adventuring offered to teach him and his brother, and when the boys were orphaned they set off for Greyhawk. Sental joined the Watch, learning city life as a constable and militiaman. His devotion to duty and natural talent soon won promotion, and his complete fearlessness helped him learn quickly. In his early thirties he became Captain of the Watch, known to all as a solid, respected citizen.

Soon after, news came that nearly broke him. His beloved brother had not joined the Watch but hired on as a caravan guard; they had tried to stay in touch, but Sental had heard nothing for a long time. Then word came through reliable channels that his brother was a prisoner in one of the Bandit Kingdoms, and soon after, that the captors wanted sensitive information about Greyhawk. If Sental refused, his brother would suffer.

The dilemma cost him many sleepless nights. He would not endanger Greyhawk, and he knew the information could seriously threaten the city in enemy hands; but he also knew the captors did not make idle threats. He decided to stall, sending information that was always out of date or as harmless as he could make it.

That worked until the captors dug their hooks in deeper. They told Sental that unless he cooperated more fully, they would tell Greyhawk's rulers that their trusted Captain was a traitor, and they had hard evidence. He had to give in. As Captain he controlled who joined the Watch and what each watchman did, and he was made to recruit men loyal to the Bandit Kingdoms and arrange their duties so they could spy at will. If the city is attacked, his orders are to put these men in charge of a stretch of wall so that the besiegers can take it more easily.

With false watchmen reporting on him, he could no longer fob the captors off with useless information, and he has had to send the best and newest he can get. He once threatened to resign, and a few days later his brother's thumb arrived at his home in a package. He knows that if his treachery is discovered, he will at the least spend a long time in Greyhawk's dungeons.

Sental is now a haggard man, tall but stooped, with thinning blond hair and a ragged beard and moustache. He chews his moustache when worried, and lately it is well chewed. He is married with three children, aged 14, 11 and 9. His wife worries about him greatly; she can see the weight on him but cannot learn what it is.

In everything his hidden masters do not control, he is an excellent Captain-General: nearly incorruptible (which is exactly why the kidnappers took his brother), fearless and always in perfect control. His liking for nonlethal weapons such as the lasso and man-catcher comes from his days as a plain watchman, when he learned that criminals were easier to bring in walking than on a stretcher, needing a cleric to heal them before trial. He does not kill needlessly and will take his quarry alive to jail when he can. Some very foolish people think that because he prefers not to kill, he will not. They are wrong.

He owns a man catcher +3, a halberd +1, a bo stick of striking (as the staff), and a shield with a symbol of hopelessness on the front behind a hinged cover he can work while using the shield, all very handy in a riot.

He is popular even with thieves and assassins, because unlike some watchmen he does not think lawbreakers exist to be killed on a whim. Even the most notorious thief or assassin will be treated as fairly as anyone else in Greyhawk, or Sental will want to know why. Any watchman he caught extorting bribes would be in serious trouble.

Player characters who want to join the Watch must prove themselves to Sental, who accepts only those he is satisfied are skilled and loyal enough. Any who learn where his brother is now will have a friend for life; he has been unable to find out exactly where in the Bandit Kingdoms his brother is held. If they bring him the information in Greyhawk, he will go straight to the Assassins' Guildmaster, Turin Deathstalker, who owes him a debt and likes him, and who would be quite willing to try to persuade the kidnappers that releasing their captive would be in their best interest. Lawbreaking characters may meet Sental professionally. He cannot be bribed, but he will treat those who try no worse than anyone else.

Thieves Guild Master-Free City of Greyhawk

AC 1 (elfin chain and dexterity bonus); MV 12"; T 14; hp 50; #AT 1; Dmg by weapon type (sling, short bow, falchion, dagger, sap); Str 13, Int 15, Wis 11, Dex 18, Con 11, Cha 16; THAC0 14; AL LN; SA quintuple damage from backstab; SD high dexterity

Org Nenshen rose in the Thieves' Guild at the same time as Nerof Gasgal, and the two often worked together. Org was on the disastrous raid when Nerof fell into a wizard's magic trap; it was Org who found him lying motionless with a look of horror on his face. Org helped pay for the clerics who restored his friend and worked tirelessly and secretly to advance Nerof's political career.

As Org rose in the Guild his name came to stand for reckless confidence and skill. When the Guildmaster died, Org was proclaimed his successor almost unanimously, and the Guild has prospered under him.

Org does not know where he was born. His parents died soon after his birth, and he was adopted by a cousin, Ramin of Greyhawk City, a greedy man who soon showed that he had taken in the boy to live in luxury on what he forced the child to steal. As Ramin should have expected, the Thieves' Guild noticed. The furious Guildmaster sent some burly thieves to bring Ramin and his young apprentice in to answer for their thefts. When Ramin finally confessed, the Guildmaster had to be held back from attacking him, and the terrified Ramin was grateful to be handed to the authorities alive. The thieves then turned to young Org. They easily won his trust and put him through a series of tests that satisfied them he had a natural gift for thieving.

So began the best part of Org's life. As a Guild apprentice he learned everything with a zeal that delighted his teachers, and he soon proved useful for squeezing through gaps too small for an adult. Before he was sixteen he was a 1st level thief, respected by his superiors and rising fast.

Meanwhile he and Nerof became firm friends and fierce competitors. They often worked together, Nerof's calm, methodical ways tempering Org's flamboyant exuberance. As the "Gruesome Twosome" they raked in loot from every victim Guild rules allowed: anyone who had not paid for protection from theft, and anyone the Guild disapproved of. Their rise was so steady that some Guild members were secretly relieved when Nerof's fear of heights pushed him into politics, since they had foreseen a bitter quarrel over who would one day be Guildmaster. Instead the Guild gained two loyal members in Greyhawk's government.

As Guildmaster, Org aims to work with the Directing Oligarchy to keep Greyhawk safe. It is the only home he has ever known, and he knows that if it fell his living would be at risk.

He is a compact, graceful man with blond hair, violet eyes and tan skin. He always dresses well and is very proud of his elven chain mail, a gift from gray elves he helped recover a stolen treasure. He practices daily at the Guild and teaches every skill to the most promising young apprentices. He owns a sling +1, a flame tongue falchion, a dagger of throwing, a cloak of the bat, a ring of jumping, boots of elvenkind and his favorite, a chime of opening. These are the rewards of a lifetime of theft, and with them he is all but unstoppable. He has ordered a new magic item, thieves' tools of opening, which has not yet been made.

For all his success, Org is secretly very insecure. He cannot quite believe how high he has risen and has always felt like a fraud, which is the real reason for his showiness: he believes that if people think he is invincible, that will make it so, whatever his talent or lack of it. His hidden fear of failure drives him to ever more daring stunts, long after most Guildmasters would be content to rest on their fame and live off their underlings' takings. Now he has a new worry as well: age. He is reaching middle age, and an aging thief often loses skill and agility. The thought terrifies him, because without his skills he believes he would be nothing but a middle-aged fraud, and he is determined to keep them as long as he can.

His friends are worried. He is taking ever greater risks and will not always beat the odds. His victims are tired of being robbed again and again and keep improving their security with more traps, better and newer locks, and magical defenses; he has even had to overcome a few lesser guardian daemons summoned by unscrupulous wizards to protect their property. The most worried is Lord Mayor Nerof Gasgal, who often bitterly regrets that his vertigo forced him into politics. He believes that if he were Org's partner again, his caution would balance Org's showiness and might keep his friend alive longer. He has resigned himself to hearing one day that Org finally pushed his luck once too often.

Assassins Guild Master-Free City of Greyhawk

AC 5 (elfin chain mail); MV 12"; F 15; hp 79; #AT 1; Dmg by weapon type (bastard sword, long bow, short bow, short sword, dagger, sling); Str 15, Int 14, Wis 10, Dex 13, Con 14, Cha 16; THAC0 6; AL LE (strong LN tendencies)

Turin Deathstalker, Master of the Guild of Assassins, is feared and respected far beyond Greyhawk. He may be the highest-ranking assassin on all Oerth and has informal authority over assassins almost everywhere. Other political forces make that authority nominal at best, but no assassin willingly goes against his known wishes.

He was born in the Shield Lands, on the border of the Horned Society. His father, a low-ranking soldier of the local lord, hoped his son would be educated, but fate stepped in. When Turin Birdstalker (his birth name) was ten, a great Horned Society army struck the Shield Lands, and he was one of many prisoners marched into the Society's lands. As far as he knows, the rest of his family was killed.

When the prisoners were shared out, he became the slave of a half-orc fighter, chief of an important orc tribe. For years he was made to do every foul task the tribe could think of, until his master decided he showed promise and began teaching him assassination. Turin was very bright and learned quickly. His teacher was pleased and amazed that the young human bore him no grudge for his years of slavery, and taught him everything he knew. Turin's first job as a full assassin was to kill the hobgoblin chief of a rival tribe, which he did gladly, having heard that the Horned Society's hobgoblin soldiers killed his family.

He seemed to have settled into life among the orcs, but he never showed his true feelings: he hated them. They came to take him for granted, and he spent several years absorbing everything the scarred old half-orc could teach. When he reached the orcish rank of Waghalter, he judged the time ripe for revenge. One fine sunny day he methodically assassinated every orc in the tribe, saving his teacher for last. Then Turin Deathstalker, as his teacher had renamed him, walked away with the tribe's wealth over his shoulder to accept an offer from a high-ranking member of the Horned Society at Molag. Turin Deathstalker never forgets a grudge.

At Molag he proved an excellent weapon for his new patron. He learned the intrigues of the Society's leaders, an incredibly tangled web of betrayal and double-cross, and grew greatly in skill, killing anyone his patron saw as an enemy and mastering disguise, poison and spying. By the time his patron was assassinated, Turin was a Senior Assassin, known to many guilds as a worthy recruit. Of the guilds that bid for him he chose Greyhawk's, and he has lived in the city ever since. Like every member he swore never to kill another member of the Assassins' Guild or anyone under its protection. The Directing Oligarchy soon hired him for several extremely dangerous and delicate missions, and when a mezzodaemon conjured by a mad wizard wiped out the Guild's upper ranks, he became Guildmaster.

As Guildmaster he aims to keep the Guild active, attract promising recruits, give them the best training possible and keep the Guild out of quarrels with other guilds and powerful groups in the city. As a member of the Directing Oligarchy he heads Greyhawk's intelligence network, and no one knows more about events in places like Iuz, the Great Kingdom and even the Scarlet Brotherhood.

He looks like a typical Shield Lander, with olive skin, red-brown hair and pale gray eyes. He practices his skills constantly and has a hundred disguises, from orc soldier to wise old sage, collecting magic items to support them. He keeps three regular disguises in Greyhawk and runs a business under each, a locksmith's shop, a servants' agency and a pawnshop, which serve his Guildsmen in many ways and earn him money. He has three mistresses, one for each disguise, and none suspects who he really is. He owns a cloak of invisibility, a dagger of venom, a short sword +2 (+5 against humanoids), boots of striding and springing, a ring of regeneration, and a quiver of arrows of humanoid slaying he ordered from a wizard.

If he has a fault, it is bitterness. He did not choose to be an assassin, and though it has brought him wealth and power, he often wishes the hobgoblins had killed him with his family. Sometimes he vanishes from Greyhawk for days and returns tired and filthy but plainly satisfied: he flies a one-man carpet of flying to the Pomarj or some other humanoid-infested land and goes on a killing spree. He has slaughtered whole tribes of hobgoblins, goblins and orcs and means to go on. His is the only guild in Greyhawk that bars half-orcs.

Apart from this obsession with killing humanoids, a special kind of murderous mania, he is not a bad man. He enjoys relaxing with his senior assassins over mugs of mead until the small hours, or seeing to city business with the rest of the Oligarchy. Despite his alignment (which leans toward lawful neutral) and his profession, he is very fond of children and vividly remembers being a helpless slave of the orcs. When he learns that someone is treating children cruelly, he has been known to set the Assassins' Guild on them. They are warned first; if they do not change their ways, the assassins end their cruelty for good.

Master of the Traders Union-Free City of Greyhawk

AC 3 (antique bronze plate mail + shield); MV 6"; F/MU 7/7; hp 58; #AT 3/2; Dmg by weapon or spell type (bastard sword, long bow, dagger, mace); Str 17, Int 17, Wis 10, Dex 17, Con 18, Cha 16; THAC0 14; AL CN; SA Spells: 4-1st, 3-2nd, 2-3rd, l-4th; SD as half-elf

Ren o' the Star was born of an affair between a human merchant's daughter and an elven noble of Celene. His mother loved him and raised him alone with her father's help, and when Ren was two she married a merchant she had known since childhood. Between his stepfather's careful training, his father's influence (he visited his father regularly) and his grandfather's advice, he chose to study both magic and swordsmanship.

As he grew he showed the mark of his father's noble house, a reddish star-shaped birthmark on his shoulder, which gave him his nickname. His proper name in human tongues is Ren Shan Fitsparaleen, showing his illegitimate tie to the elven House of Paraleen. With the combined wealth of his father, stepfather and mother he had the best tutors, and like most half-elves he was an excellent student, combining the best of both bloodlines.

When he came of age, an inheritance from his grandfather let him start a business trading furs, ivory and precious metals, anything valuable and compact. He would buy something bulky at an irresistible price, but the trouble of moving and guarding bulky goods to a good market made him wary of it. He soon saw that Greyhawk was the hub of trade on Oerth, and once he had built a respectable fortune he moved there and joined the Traders' Union. His knowledge of the region and his ties to both human and elven communities made him valuable, and he soon became a rich, respected trader with ventures all over Oerth.

Success brought trouble. Envious people resented the "half-breed's" good fortune and tried everything from magical scrying of his plans to outright assassination, even bribing bandits and humanoids to attack his caravans. Whenever Ren found out who was responsible, he struck back, and in time the survivors spread word that he was no easy mark. Eventually he was made a Master of the Traders' Union, fulfilling one of his life's ambitions.

He takes strongly after his elven father: 5'9", with black hair, upswept eyebrows, pointed ears and a thick moustache. He is very proud of his antique bronze plate mail, which he got from a tribe of barbarians who found it looting an ancient ruin. He persuaded them to trade it for a wonderful horse, and a magnificent beast it was, since he had made sure of that when he polymorphed it from a monkey a few hours earlier. When the barbarians found the horse gone they naturally searched Ren's camp, but no one connected the missing steed with the little monkey sitting so innocently on his shoulder.

He also owns a wand of lightning won in a dice game, gauntlets of swimming and climbing, a necklace of adaptation and a folding boat. His magic weapons include a longbow of speed, a bastard sword of sharpness, and a cursed sword +1 that he sometimes sells for cash, knowing it will come back. The sword of sharpness has intelligence 14 and chaotic neutral alignment, detects precious metals and gems, and argues with Ren constantly. "Some people are hen-pecked," he moans, "but I'm sword-pecked!" His old trading partners are used to seeing him walk along arguing with his sword.

His great weakness is gambling. In the old days, crossing half of Oerth on trading ventures satisfied his taste for risk and made him money; he gambled then, but mostly in small dice games with his partners, and kept his losses well within his means. In Greyhawk, with little to amuse him but counting his gold, the urge has taken over. He spends endless hours in Nerof Gasgal's gaming house and others, bets on horse races and elections, and his friends have been amazed to see him seriously trying to bet on which of two flies will take off first. Perhaps he thinks he is too rich to be hurt by his losses. He is not: he is rich, but not infinitely so, and he has already run through an incredible amount. His friends have tried to warn him, but he brushes them off, while Nerof and the other gaming-house owners love him, since his money is pouring into their pockets.

GA p.40. Rewritten in plain words; statistics as printed. The armor class, THAC0 and damage are as printed; the sheet works out its own from the class, abilities and equipment.

The Mage of the Vale, the Exalted Mage, the Black One-Valley of the Mage

AC 2 (bracers of defense, AC 2); MV 12"; MU 19; hp 55; #AT 1; Dmg by weapon or spell type; Str 8, Int 19, Wis 9, Dex 17, Con 15, Cha 13; THAC0 13; AL NE; SA spells; SD spells, high Intelligence; 5-1st, 5-2nd, 5-3rd, 5-4th, 5-5th, 3-6th, 37th, 3-8th, l-9th

The Laird of the Valley of the Mage is a mystery to the outside world. Few have spoken with him, and fewer still lived to tell of it. Supposed eyewitnesses do not even agree on what he looks like or how he talks, so either people are lying or he disguises himself with spells at least some of the time.

He was born far from his valley, in the capital of the Great Kingdom. As Jaran Krimeeah he was a relative of the Great King and was given the best magical training the kingdom could buy. As his skill and power grew, he became discontented. Why, he asked himself, should his cousin, who could not cast a single 1st level spell, be king? Jaran saw wizards as the elite of humankind, whose wonderful powers ought to make them rulers everywhere.

So the young wizard gathered his forces and tried to seize power. Unfortunately his skill at magic far exceeded his skill at palace politics. The commanders he had won over turned out to have little real authority; when they gave orders, the soldiers checked with higher authority and were told not to obey. The whole sorry affair collapsed almost as soon as it began. The royal family did not execute him. Instead they exiled him, making him swear never to reveal his relation to them and never to return to or meddle in the Great Kingdom again.

Cast out into a hard world, Jaran, now calling himself the Black One, easily found work in the Bandit Kingdoms casting spells for their crude rulers. He came to believe that agents of the Great Kingdom were hunting him, grew obsessed with magical defenses against unseen enemies, and left his post to devote himself wholly to magical research. He traveled through the Shield Lands, the Horned Society, Furyondy, Veluna, Keoland, the Yeomanry and Sterich, always seeking more spells and lore. At last, in the Grand Duchy of Geoff, he found the hidden valley he now rules. "Here," he told himself, "is what I've been looking for. A safe, secure, hidden base, easily defended and not claimed by anybody who cares about it. If I take this place over, I'll finally be able to pursue my research in peace!"

He quickly won over the valley elves and the local gnomes, and when he hinted as delicately as he could that he might make a better overlord than the distant, uncaring Grand Duke of Geoff, they proclaimed him their Laird unanimously. With their eager help he fortified the valley's entrance heavily, both physically and magically. Secure at last, he gave himself almost entirely to research, letting the elves and gnomes run their own affairs and handling only the problems they could not.

He is a tall, thin man with kinky brown hair, pale olive skin and slate-colored eyes. He cares only for his research and for new spells, and tends to treat anyone who cannot cast spells as feeble-minded. He is so sure of the superiority of spellcasters, wizards above all, that he will not even use a weapon, scorning daggers, darts and nonmagical staves as unworthy of a mage.

His obsession has led him into great danger. Whenever he hears of a spellbook with a spell he does not know, he will go to almost any length for it, even teleporting into a ruined city to fight a lich. He is so consumed with the desire to work magic that he is even preparing to cheat death, though not as a lich, since he thinks any kind of undeath unworthy of a mage. He plans to work until his body begins to seriously decline and then become a shade by filling his body with shadowstuff from the Plane of Shadow. As a shade he could never rise in level, but living for centuries to do more research seems a small price, especially since he means to be 24th level by then.

He owns dozens of spellbooks and a great store of magic items, among them rings of feather falling, spell turning, spell storing and wizardry, a staff of the magi, a wand of fire, a wand of frost, a book of infinite spells, a cloak of displacement, a special deck of many things with no good cards at all ("Pick a card, any card!"), a gem of seeing, a mirror of life trapping and a hat of disguise. These are only the items he is known to have; there are probably many more.

He is obsessed with agents of the Great Kingdom and considers every outsider in his valley a possible agent sent to harm him, hence his fixation on defenses and his wish to become a shade. He keeps a large network of assassins, mostly valley elves passing as humans, in the lands outside. They do various tasks, such as hunting old enemies, but their main job is the endless search for agents of the Great Kingdom. If he were ever convinced that no such agents existed, he would be devastated.

First Protector-Valley of the Mage

AC 4 (bracers of defense, AC 4); MV 12"; MU 8; hp 35; #AT 1; Dmg by weapon type (staff of striking, dagger); Str 12, Int 20, Wis 9, Dex 13, Con 17, Cha 13; THAC0 19; AL CN; SA as female dark elf, Spells: 4-1st, 3-2nd, 3-3rd, 2-4th, l-5th, and special; SD as female dark elf.

Tysiln San was born in the Vault of the Drow to a family of merchants, who trained her in magic and expected her to spend her life with them. She was utterly loyal to her kin, and when they began plotting to overthrow the priestesses of Lolth, she gave them her full support. The plot failed and the rebellion was crushed almost before it began. Fleeing for her life, she met a human wizard who had come to the Vault on magical business, threw herself on his mercy, and he agreed to take her back to the surface.

Nothing in her upbringing had prepared her for the surface world. For several weeks she suffered from agoraphobia, a fear of wide open spaces, and would not go outdoors. The wizard helped her overcome it and gave her a pair of magic lenses, made by a master mirror maker so that the wearer can see through them while from outside they look like mirrors; he cast glassteel on them to make them nearly unbreakable. With them she could manage in bright sunlight as well as in darkness. For several years she helped the wizard with his experiments, until one went badly wrong. He tried to create a variation of the gate spell and thought he had succeeded, but his first attempt to gate in a hierarch modron brought a froglike death slaad instead, which promptly killed him and tried to kill her. Only her drow power to levitate saved her.

Alone on the surface for the first time, she wandered for several years. She settled for a while in a halfling community, casting spells such as mending in return for food and shelter, then roamed many lands until a patrol of valley elves caught her in the Dim Forest. Brought before the Mage of the Valley, she fell madly in love. He was still consolidating his rule, and the sudden arrival of a skilled wizard who adored him seemed a gift from the gods. Once he was sure of her loyalty, he gave her her freedom on condition that she pass a series of ever more dangerous tests. She passed them all and became his mistress and his most trusted servant at once.

She is an exquisitely beautiful drow woman with long, straight white hair, white upswept eyebrows, huge yellow eyes, delicate features and black skin. She knows how beautiful she is and will use that, or anything else she has, in the Mage's service. To her, the Mage decides right and wrong. She is utterly loyal to him and madly in love. She knows he would sacrifice her without a second thought to gain his ends, and this does not trouble her. She looks forward to his becoming a shade, since she thinks his only flaws are his pale skin and his short human life.

Besides her mirrored lenses she owns elven boots, a cloak of arachnida (a souvenir of her family's revolt against Lolth's priestesses), a bag of holding, a wand of lightning, a ring of elemental command and a staff of striking. She has full use of her lover's spellbooks and her old master's. Having learned from her master's fate, she keeps a set of scrolls of protection against demons, devils, lycanthropes, snakes and undead.

She is now First Protector of the Valley of the Mage. She begged her lover for a responsible post, and he put her in charge of the valley's guards. She took command of the gnomes and valley elves who guarded the entrance and set to work with an intensity that astonished the Mage. She laid out inviting paths studded with subtle but deadly traps, paths that looked impassable but led straight into the valley, and hidden posts where gnome and valley elf assassins could watch the paths and ambush intruders. She hardly changed the look of the entrance, but any enemy now gets warned away by magic mouths in unexpected, inventive places, frightened off by illusions cast by gnome spellcasters, or killed if they keep coming.

Her own post is at the narrowest, most heavily fortified point of the entrance. Anyone who gets that far is challenged by a huge statue nearby, which announces by magic mouth: "Stop at the station and state your business!" It is made to look like a stone golem, and gnome spellcasters make it seem to move to strengthen the illusion. Tysiln questions intruders to see if they have good reason to be there. The less she likes their answers, the more she flirts with them to distract them, while a real, invisible stone golem waits for her signal to crush them. She uses her drow powers of clairvoyance, detect lie, know alignment and suggestion to learn their business. If she is satisfied they have legitimate business, she guides them through the entrance and past the traps.

The Father of Obedience-The Scarlet Brotherhood

AC -2; MV 30"; MK 16; hp 60; #AT 4/1; Dmg 5-30 or by weapon type + 8; Str 17, Int 11, Wis 16, Dex 17, Con 18, Cha 13; THAC0 10; AL LE; SA as 16th level monk; SD as 16th level monk.

Korenth Zan was born among the Scarlet Brotherhood, a product of the selective breeding program begun by the first Father of Obedience. His father was an evil fighter in the Brotherhood's service and his mother an assassin. He knew them, but the Brotherhood raised him, and both died fighting its enemies, so he sees the Brotherhood as his true family.

As a child he was tested again and again to find his strengths, and was judged to have what a monk needs. For fifteen years he trained hard, learning the Brotherhood's beliefs along with monkish skills. In his youth he led every kind of childish mischief, from midnight raids on the pantries to vandalizing the rooms of unpopular teachers. This pleased his trainers, who decided he had just the kind of leadership the Brotherhood needed.

When his training ended he was sent out into the world with a mixed party of Brotherhood servants to gather treasure for their leaders and thwart the order's enemies. For years these evil adventurers traveled, killing good creatures for their treasure, helping the Brotherhood's allies and learning much about the world beyond its stronghold. Korenth soon led the group, and his cunning saved them many times. He rose quickly through the ranks of monks, defeating a host of foes with his martial arts.

When the survivors reached about 10th level they returned to the Brotherhood laden with gifts and information. Their knowledge of the outside world made their advice sought after, and all his old companions were soon high in the Brotherhood's councils. Korenth went back to the monastery and set out to rise above them all. He fought and beat challengers as needed to gain or hold rank until he became a Master of Spring, and rose at the same time through the Brotherhood to become Father of Obedience.

He is an average-sized man with a shaved head (required by his order), pale skin and black eyes. He is completely loyal to the Brotherhood and works tirelessly to advance its aims, spending much of his time overseeing its activities and nearly all the rest training new monks and keeping himself in training. At lower levels he used many weapons and became proficient with hand axe, bo stick, club, crossbow, dagger, javelin, jo stick, spear and falchion. He still practices with each daily to set an example, but scorns weapons in real combat. He owns a club +5, a crossbow of accuracy +3, a ring of invisibility and a ring of marid summoning.

As Father of Obedience he is suspicious of his subordinates, suspecting them of ambition and of plotting to replace him. Some secretly think his mind is failing and that he will slide into paranoid madness. His subordinates are still loyal, but his accusations of treason, usually followed by the swift execution of the "traitors," are shaking their loyalty. In time the imaginary traitors will become real, and he will have sealed his own fate. When he is not hunting traitors he is an excellent administrator, checking his subordinates' work so often that they dare not dawdle or make avoidable mistakes. In fact, many of the "traitors" he thinks he has caught were just ordinary underlings who had made some error.

He counts everyone outside the Brotherhood as an actual or potential enemy. In his years abroad he heard enough ill said of the Brotherhood to convince him that outsiders were plotting against it, and often he is right: there are plenty of plots against it, mostly because it is seen as a great danger to all of Oerth.

He is unmarried but has fathered several children through the breeding program. Since no member of the Brotherhood may have children any other way, he thinks this normal and would be very surprised to hear it called wrong. He has sneered at outsiders who dared criticize it: "You of the outside take more care breeding dogs than you do in breeding your own descendants! And then you wonder why we of the Brotherhood are so powerful!" His children include an evil 3rd level fighter, an assassin and two monks. He is enormously proud of them but never shows it in public, since that would go against the Brotherhood's principles, and he is a stickler for principle. His present mistress is an evil wizard in the Brotherhood's service. She knows that using her spells on any high official, let alone the Father of Obedience, would mean an unpleasant death, so she relies only on her looks and charm to keep his affection. Like all monks he is lawful and does not hold with casual affairs.

As long as he avoids falling into paranoia, Korenth Zan will go on leading the Scarlet Brotherhood.

Member, First Order-The Scarlet Brotherhood

AC 6; MV 20"; MK 6; hp 32; #AT 1 or 3/2; Dmg 2-8 or by weapon type + 3; Str 15, Int 10, Wis 17, Dex 18, Con 18, Cha 9; THAC0 18; AL LE; SA as 6th level monk; SD as 6th level monk.

Alesh Marin is a product of the Scarlet Brotherhood's breeding program, the child of two high-level monks. Like Korenth Zan, she tested as having a monk's abilities and was trained at the Brotherhood's training center, where her record was competent but unremarkable. Her training ended recently, and as is the custom she was sent out with a mixed group of young Brotherhood members to prove herself. The Brotherhood thinks knowledge of the outside world and the chance of treasure are well worth the high risk that many of these young people will never return.

She is now in Stoink, in the Bandit Kingdoms, as an innkeeper's mistress. She is the only survivor of her original group and has several powerful magic items. Her favorite method is to talk a wealthy-looking adventurer into letting her join his party, then wait for a chance to make off with whatever treasure she can carry. She is determined to gain power and dreams of one day being the first female "Father" of Obedience. When not adventuring she trains in her room at the inn or works as a barmaid and bouncer in its common room. She will stay as long as she believes the innkeeper really has the big chest of gold he is always boasting of, or as long as he can keep convincing her that the mythical chest exists.

She is slender, with short blond hair, blue eyes and white skin. She succeeds as a bouncer partly because the bullies who drink in Stoink do not want to be seen thrown out of a door or window by a woman. She became head barmaid by framing the woman who held the job: "evidence" turned up that the old head barmaid was skimming from the till, and she was fired. Unfortunately Alesh did not know her rival was the sister of Stoink's Assassins' Guildmaster. He was furious when he learned why his sister was dismissed, and he has worked out that Alesh is a monk of the Scarlet Brotherhood, but he will not take his revenge until he thinks of a suitably hideous way.

Her main weakness is that she is an incurable schemer. Offered a simple solution or a complicated, sneaky plan that involves stabbing some of her "friends" in the back, she takes the second every time, because she enjoys it, and she studies ways to improve her technique. She was once the mistress of an assassin until she had learned all he could teach her about poison, whereupon she poisoned him and ran off with his belongings. She sees other people as objects: things to satisfy her wants, or obstacles to remove on her way up. She cannot always keep this out of her words and manner, hence her fairly low charisma; most people not blinded by her beauty distrust her and treat her like a poisonous snake. She is rightly suspected of causing her companions' deaths. Rumor of this has reached the Brotherhood, and her superiors plan to harness her ambition for their own use.

Her ambitions are fed by her magic items: a ring of three wishes, a stone of good luck and a clear spindle ioun stone (which sustains her without food or water). Her weapons include a dagger of venom and a bardiche +2. She has built on what her late lover taught her about poisons until she is as skilled with them as an alchemist or high-level assassin.

She keeps in touch with the Brotherhood through a low-level fighter who runs its spy network around Stoink, sending regular reports to headquarters and always sounding like a willing tool of her leaders, though the only leader who would truly please her is herself. She does not know that the fighter also sends reports on her from other sources, with his own notes added, so she is unaware that the Brotherhood's leaders know of her disloyalty.

Her ultimate ambitions go far beyond becoming the first female Father of Obedience. She is sure she would rule Oerth far better than its present rulers and plans to use her hoped-for leadership of the Brotherhood to spread her rule over more lands. Eventually, she thinks, she could extend the breeding program to produce a perfect race combining the supposed superiority of the Suel with the undeniable numbers of other races.

She is grim and driven and seldom smiles unless some treachery of hers especially amuses her. The last time she smiled, she had just lured a man carrying money into embracing her so she could draw her dagger of venom and stab him in the back. She is utterly despicable and will never change by choice. She likes being evil and prefers it to good, feeling that only evil gives a person of her talents room to shine. She will pretend to be good if the deception gains her something, but shows her true colors as soon as she has what she wants. She hates all her superiors, even those who have done her good turns, simply because they have what she wants.

Duke-Duchy of Urnst

AC -5 (full plate armor +4 and shield +1); MV 6"; R 12; hp 71; #AT 3/2; Dmg by weapon type (specialized with longbow; proficient with two-handed sword, halberd, long sword, dagger, battle axe); Str 16, Int 14, Wis 14, Dex 14, Con 17, Cha 17; THAC0 10; AL CG; SA spells, as 12th level ranger

Karll was the youngest of the six children of the last Duke and Duchess of Urnst. From his earliest years he loved the outdoors. Since he was not expected to inherit, his parents were delighted when a family friend offered to have him trained as a ranger, and Karll was so eager that he was packed almost before they finished telling him. The Duchy is home to the only ranger school in the world, and Karll became its best pupil, quickly mastering tracking and fighting giant-class creatures. He was made a Runner at 21, the earliest possible age.

For the next twenty years or so young Lord Karll (a courtesy title from his father) lived in bliss. He took easily to his teachers' lessons about crusading endlessly against evil in every form, especially giants and humanoids. Being chaotic good, he was an individualist and would vanish into the wilderness alone for months at a time, coming back tired, dusty and travel-stained with a string of fresh trophies for his peers and a few words of news for his superiors.

Meanwhile things went badly for his family. His eldest brothers died in a border war with desert nomad raiders, and his two sisters were assassinated by unknown enemies (a neighboring lord who had been refused both their hands was suspected). When his last surviving brother became Duke on their father's death, he was suffering from wounds and did not have long to live. So, much to his surprise and displeasure, Karll was called back from the rangers and groomed to rule as the only heir. He had never expected to be Duke, had no training for it, and hated giving up the carefree life of the forests. He almost had to be dragged home, and only a direct order from his ranger superiors stopped him from renouncing the title and going back to the woods.

He decided to make the best of it. He improved the army's weapons, armor and training, brought in many rangers to train the troops, and did much of the training himself, passing on his woodcraft and tracking. But he cares about his duchy mainly as a base for his endless war on evil. He is impatient with the daily business of government and has become a magnet for scoundrels. He naively believes others mean as well as he does, and with no training in rule he has surrounded himself with the biggest crowd of thieves outside the Bandit Kingdoms.

As a result the Duchy is badly ruled. Court verdicts go to whoever bribes the judges most, the peasants are taxed and cheated, and their daughters are carried off at the whim of anyone in authority. The peasants blame the Duke's corrupt advisers, not the Duke himself. Petitioners who try to tell him how his people really live are threatened by mysterious bandits, and persistent protesters have been assassinated. If he were not so obsessed with his crusade he would probably notice and act drastically, but his advisers deliberately keep him in the dark.

Duke Karll is tall, strong and handsome, tanned by a life outdoors, with brown hair and icy green eyes. He specialized in the bow early in his career and owns a long bow +4 and a quiver of arrows of slaying evil beings. He is immensely proud of two family heirlooms, a suit of full plate armor +4 and a shield +1. He also owns a flame tongue two-handed sword, a cloak of displacement taken from an evil wizard's body, a ring of regeneration and gauntlets of ogre power. He values magic items exactly as far as they help fight evil and would happily trade his crown, orb or scepter for an item made to kill evil humanoids and giants. He has a fairly complete set of spellbooks but uses them only to relearn the spells he knows.

His ultimate goal is to launch a grand crusade against evil, above all evil giants and humanoids. He is reasonable on most subjects, but tell him this is impossible or unwise and he flies into a wild rage. Though many duties of government need him, he still disappears into the forests for days at a time to hunt them. He does not understand that what is good in a ranger is not necessarily good in a ruler; he sees the Duchy as a base for his crusade and cannot be convinced that his duties as Duke come before his duties as a ranger. His subjects like him, but they know he would sacrifice them if it meant protecting a greater number from evil, and not surprisingly they resent it. Unless things change, Duke Karll is doomed. At his ministers' urging he is looking for a wife, but cannot understand why neighboring rulers seem reluctant to trust him with their daughters.

Prince of the Clan-Dry Steppes

AC 6 (padded armor, shield, and dexterity bonus); MV 12"; F 12; hp 80; #AT 3/2; Dmg by weapon type; Str 16, Int 12, Wis 8, Dex 15, Con 16, Cha 13; THAC0 10; AL CN

Tang the Horrific, Tarkhan of the Purple Eagle Tribe, was born in a yurt on the Dry Steppes and had an ordinary steppe boyhood: riding almost before he could walk, shooting the bow, hunting and raiding neighboring tribes. Unlike other nomad boys he was restless and wanted to see the wonders of the rest of Oerth, if only to inspire his people to fall on the settled peoples and conquer them. His father, the Kha-Khan of their tribe, gave him his blessing to travel among the settled nations, along with a one-man yurt, a Bactrian camel and a string of strong nomad ponies.

Since then Tang, nicknamed "the Horrific" by the first civilized people he met, has roamed Oerth as a mercenary. He still will not live indoors and pitches his yurt wherever he can. He has served many masters, good and evil: for a while he trained the cavalry of several lords of the Shield Lands, and he has served in places as different as Iuz, the Great Kingdom, Greyhawk, Furyondy and Tenh. Between jobs he rode with bands of bold adventurers on raids.

He is now between jobs and living on his savings, his yurt pitched in the Shield Lands, expecting some local lord unhappy with his light cavalry to call on him soon. Meanwhile he relaxes as he likes best: riding his pony, practicing archery and scimitar work, and learning new woodlore. He is skilled with knife, spear, hand axe, scimitar, short bow, horseman's flail, spiked buckler, light lance, dagger and javelin. He has his people's barbarian skills: cliff climbing, hiding in natural surroundings, surprise, back protection, leaping and springing, detecting illusion and magic, leadership, survival, first aid, outdoor craft, tracking, animal handling, horsemanship, long-distance signaling and yurt building. He dislikes magic and uses no magic weapons, thinking them unworthy of a true Tarkhan.

For all his years among civilized folk he is still a barbarian and holds fast to his people's ways, especially the vendetta. Whatever his alignment, once he has sworn enmity against someone he will do anything in his power to bring them grief.

He is a short, bandy-legged man with a round, flat face, a snub nose, gray-streaked black hair and black slanted eyes. He is nearly always smiling and is very friendly to anyone he knows is not evil or tied to Iuz and his allies. He reads, speaks several languages fluently, and owns many maps of Oerth, which he pores over constantly, trying to work out how a horde of steppe nomads could reach Iuz without crossing so much hostile land.

He has some barbarian quirks and taboos. He will not willingly sleep anywhere but in a yurt, a tent or the open; forced to spend a night indoors, he feels trapped and often has terrible nightmares. A personal taboo forbids him to ride anything but a horse or a camel; donkeys, elephants, vehicles and other ways of travel are off limits.

He left Iuz under a dark cloud and is consumed with mad hatred for it. He has sworn a vendetta against Iuz and attacks any evil humanoid he sees, believing it an agent of Iuz. Ask him what he most wants and he will talk for hours about bringing a huge horde of his people, with the Rovers of the Barrens and the Tiger and Wolf Nomads as allies, to lay waste to Iuz's whole kingdom and kill every creature in it. If he can find a way, he will go home to raise a horde of his own folk to ruin Iuz.

This obsession is unusual in so friendly, easygoing a man. It began while he commanded Iuz's cavalry as a mercenary. Scornful of "civilized" folk, he did not much mind riding with Iuz's horsemen against settled peoples, but when Iuz wanted to send him and his command against the Rovers of the Barrens, Tang rebelled. The Rovers were too much like his own people, and he could not bring himself to slaughter them. Iuz ordered his arrest, but Tang talked his cavalry into killing the messengers and defected with them to the Wolf Nomads. His defiance threw Iuz into a raving fury. Iuz has never stopped searching for him, and if Tang were ever brought before him he could expect no mercy. Iuz had meant to use the cavalry Tang was training against the nomads on his northern borders, and seeing those nomads strengthened by his own men enraged him.

Tang is unmarried, since he does not think "civilized" girls fit company for a Tarkhan of the Purple Eagle Clan. He is very good at repairing his yurt and makes excellent kumiss (fermented milk). He is always glad to see fellow nomads and will happily sit up till the small hours talking shop, arguing over which bow is best, discussing horses or comparing hunting methods. He is an excellent general in the nomad style, used to commanding every kind of troops. Iuz is right to see him as a threat: if he brings a horde of his people to Iuz along with the northern nomads, little could stand against him but the cities, which would starve without supplies.

Magic-User-Great Kingdom

AC 3 (bracers of defense, AC 3); MV 12"; MU 6; hp 19; #AT 1; Dmg by weapon or spell type (staff, dart, dagger); Str 4, Int 17, Wis 13, Dex 12, Con 9, Cha 8; THAC0 19; AL CN; SA spells: 4-1st, 2-2nd, 2-3rd; SD magic items

Timitrios Spartakos was born in Rauxes, capital of the Great Kingdom, to shabby but genteel parents. His father had been a minor noble until a relative's conviction for treason ruined the family. Timitrios grew up on the streets until a family friend used influence to get him taken on as a pupil of the great Jaran Krimeeah, a relative of the Imperial family who could pick and choose his students. With a street child's cynicism, Timitrios waited to learn what his good fortune would cost.

He found out the first night. An agent of the Imperial Secret Police, posing as Jaran's butler, questioned him in his room and made him agree to report any suspicious talk. Jaran was politically suspect as a royal relative; the secret police had him closely but quietly watched, and the arrogant wizard did not seem to notice. There was evidence he was plotting a coup, and he would most likely confide in his apprentice. Timitrios was to report everything.

The boy took to his double life with glee. He enjoyed the spiteful power of fooling the Empire's foremost wizard, and liked being a secret agent whose messages high officials read. As expected, Jaran began plotting and, unable to resist bragging, confided every step to his apprentice. Timitrios quickly learned how to draw him out, and his reports gave the plot in exact detail. When Jaran was arrested, Timitrios was a chief witness. Locked in plate armor (the Great Kingdom's custom for wizards on trial), Jaran listened helplessly as his traitorous apprentice laid out the whole plot. When he was convicted, he screamed threats of revenge against everyone he blamed for his fall, Timitrios above all.

After Jaran was exiled, the Secret Police gave their favorite spy an amulet of proof against location (later called an amulet of proof against detection), since an angry wizard could easily take revenge, and arranged for him to study with a famous wizard. His new teacher was unworldly and paid little attention to his pupils outside class, so they were left to themselves, and Timitrios took to drinking, just for fun, he said. When he learned that some fellow pupils were using their arts unlawfully, he turned it to his advantage, and with a clever mix of tattling to the Secret Police and backstabbing he soon had them all afraid of him. He stayed on good terms with his master, and by quietly smoothing over a small scandal involving his teacher and a pretty serving girl, won his gratitude. Only his magical talent kept him from being his master's prize pupil.

When his master died, Timitrios inherited a box of maps said to show where treasures lay. He moved to Greyhawk, since the treasures were near there, and to get away from people who remembered his betrayals. His bad name had not followed him, and he easily found work. But in Greyhawk he began drinking heavily, often spending weeks in a stupor and staggering out only when his drink ran low. At last he noticed his savings running out and managed to sober up.

Now 27, he has black hair, olive skin and black eyes, is of average height, and usually wears ordinary street clothes rather than wizard's robes. His familiar, a calico cat, is never far away. Besides his amulet he owns a ring of spell storing that belonged to his last teacher, holding only defensive spells (feather fall, invisibility, protection from normal missiles and teleport), two potions of treasure finding, a ring of protection +2, a wand of negation, boots of speed, an efreeti bottle, and two ioun stones, one pale lavender and one lavender and green (absorbing spells of up to 4th and 8th level), all taken from his two powerful former masters.

The Mage of the Valley has not forgotten the pupil who betrayed him. His valley elf assassins are watching for Timitrios, and once the Mage learns exactly where he is, he means to pay him a visit to "talk over old times together." Ugly rumors are also spreading in Greyhawk about the young wizard from the Great Kingdom. He has slipped back into drink several times and bungled several jobs while drunk. He refuses clerical help, insisting he is fine, but people who want a reliable spellcaster are more and more reluctant to hire the dark young man from Rauxes. Asked, he would probably go with a party of adventurers to the places on his treasure maps, but he would very likely (90%) take "his share" one night and leave.

Cleric-The Horned Society

AC 3 (banded mail + shield); MV 9"; C 8; hp 50; #AT 1; Dmg by weapon or spell type (mace, staff, staff sling, club); Str 10, Int 11, Wis 16, Dex 18, Con 14, Cha 18; THAC0 16; AL LE; SA Spells: 5-1st, 5-2nd, 3-3rd, 2-4th; SD spells

Guiliana Mortidus was born to members of the Horned Society, an evil fighter mother and an evil priest father, who dedicated her to the Society before she was born. When she was old enough she was tested exhaustively, showed the makings of a cleric, and began training at the earliest possible age. She was not popular: her sneering contempt for the less gifted and her talent for holding a grudge left her few friends. She moved through the school exactly on schedule without showing any special talent, doing the menial tasks given to pupils without complaint but without enthusiasm, and on finishing was invested as a cleric.

She hid her burning hatreds from her superiors and teachers, judging that they would betray her to her enemies, and raged in secret that she could not yet crush everyone who had ever offended her. When she was given a low-ranking post in the Society's temples, she smiled politely, accepted and bided her time. After several years she was made a clerical "adviser" to the Society's armies, which were preparing for war, and went off happily, watching for ways to advance. She gained experience quickly, and a few magic items of no great worth; the valuable ones always went to the high command, and seeing them flaunt things she wanted made her blood boil.

At last, after a battle against the Shield Landers, her patience paid off. Searching among the dead and wounded for those needing healing, she found a ring of human influence on a dead Shield Lands officer and a talisman of pure evil on a wounded, unconscious Horned Society cleric, whom she promptly killed to take it. She has used both ever since, but carefully, since she does not want anyone to know she has them; she has seen many colleagues stabbed or smothered in their sleep for their magic items and does not mean to share their fate. With the ring she has suggested to her equals that they should not stand in her way, and she has been experimenting with suggesting to her superiors that she deserves promotion.

Owning these items has made her vainer and even less popular than before. She used to be merely unbearable, with her disagreeable ways and her well-founded touchiness about her plain looks. Now she has alienated nearly everyone of equal or lower rank, and her superiors, who rightly suspect her ambition, watch her carefully. She is a thin, slovenly woman with stringy brown hair, weak features, bad teeth and faded blue eyes, who wears a battered suit of banded mail and carries a shield in battle. She does exactly what her superiors tell her and nothing more.

She has started a small spy network of her own, mostly hobgoblins who believe the Society has approved it, and plans to use what they learn to incriminate her enemies and take revenge. She does not know that a lowly potboy she recruited is really an assassin in disguise spying on her. Her superiors have no present reason to worry about her schemes but want to make sure they do not endanger them. If her plans are consistently clumsy she will be charged, condemned and executed; if they show promise she will be quietly encouraged to fit them into her superiors' larger plans.

She is now a cleric of middle rank at the Society's main temple in Molag and has gone on several minor missions to its allies, such as Iuz. She rules her few underlings by threats and abuse, and everyone unlucky enough to rank below her hates and fears her. Besides the ring and talisman she owns a staff of withering that also works as a staff sling +2, and a mace +1. She is bargaining for a set of chain mail +2 that some hobgoblins captured in a recent fight, but their shaman knows its worth and is asking a high price.

Apart from her lust for revenge, she is completely loyal to the ideals and goals of the Horned Society. Having seen so little of the outside world, she barely understands that any other view of life is possible, let alone reasonable. Secretly she thinks anyone who refuses to accept the Society's teachings is at best willfully fooling himself, if not mad. The few times she has spoken with prisoners, she could not grasp how they could hold views so opposite to hers. She will gladly argue philosophy and alignment, but nothing will convince her that the Horned Society is anything but a paradise on earth for wise souls who work hard and obey its laws.
